thread.title: Tech founders adopt utilitarian approach to private jet travel, reports say

author: beaver state news
title: Tech founders adopt utilitarian approach to private jet travel, reports say
text:
Some tech billionaires are shifting away from traditional luxury in private aviation, opting for a more utilitarian style on their Gulfstream jets, according to a Jun. 17 report. Instead of emphasizing lavish amenities, these founders are focusing on practicality by filling seats with employees and replacing high-end catering with simple snacks.
A Silicon Valley source described the trend by saying, “The founder way to make their jet seem like a utility and not a luxury is simple. Fill the seats with employees, ditch the flight attendant for Starlink, and roam the cabin picking up empty Coke cans.” The New York Post reported that food choices now often include items such as In-N-Out burgers when departing Los Angeles or bagels and deli sandwiches before leaving New York.
Another source said, “A lot of the luxuries you would expect — champagne, caviar — that doesn’t really happen very often these days,” suggesting that many of the hallmarks of airborne opulence have been set aside in favor of simpler comforts.
Despite these changes in onboard experience, observers note that flying privately remains an expensive endeavor with significant environmental impact. The article points out that even without traditional luxuries like champagne or caviar, private jets still consume large amounts of fuel and generate considerable air pollution compared to commercial flights. Operating costs can exceed $100,000 for a cross-country trip regardless of how modestly passengers behave during flight.
In response to this trend’s portrayal as functional rather than extravagant, some readers expressed skepticism in comments featured by The New York Post. One commenter wrote, “Pretending not to be about conspicuous consumption when the flight itself is the epitome of conspicuous consumption is absurd, especially when no one outside will know there’s no flight attendant on board.” Another added, “So instead of a flight attendant, it will just be one of their regular staff assistants doing the jobs.”
